alignments.note: Article surfaces as the under rule 19; split from its noun under rule 26.
Noun stands alone, its determiner having gone to the article.

Circumstantial participle expanded into a finite clause: the supplied subordinator when is a rule 7 helper on the participle (rule 86 places a supplied when on a participle, and a participle is exactly the token that licenses it), the supplied subject it and the auxiliary hath ride along under rules 7 and 9, and rule 9 heads the unit on the lexical verb conceived rather than on it or hath. The supplied subject stays with the verb whose subject it is, as rule 74 has it.
Finite verb; no helper is written for it.
Anarthrous accusative rendered by a bare sin.
Second article surfaces as the under rule 19, kept separate from its noun under rule 26.

Postpositive connective realized by and; rule 15 permits the reordering relative to the article. This is an expressed Greek conjunction, so rule 88's supplied participle-to-finite juncture is not in question.
Noun stands alone beside its own article.

Aorist passive participle expanded into a finite clause exactly as s004 is, which is rule 24's habit: when, the supplied subject it, and the copula is are helpers on the participle, and the head is the meaning-bearing fullgrown rather than the copula, under rules 9 and 17.

One verb rendered by the phrasal bringeth forth; forth is the verb's own particle and not a separate source item, as rule 36's girt with and rule 34's afar off treat an English particle. Head on bringeth: rule 91's test asks which English word the lexeme is glossed by, and ἀποκυέω is itself bring forth rather than a support verb with a contentful complement, so rule 17's make straight case does not apply. Heading on forth was the competing reading and is rejected on that ground.
Anarthrous accusative rendered by a bare death.

review_notes: Reviewed against the contract and returned unchanged: no unit's membership, status or head was altered. Two notes were expanded to cite the rules that were checked (s004 on rule 74's supplied subject, s008 on rule 88's expressed-conjunction carve-out, s011 on the particle precedent); no analysis changed.

Every s### and t### id is used exactly once; no ids invented. All twelve units are aligned with nonempty arrays and heads inside them, so rules 3-6 are satisfied and no unrepresented or added unit arises.

Both participles get identical treatment (when + supplied subject + auxiliary or copula on the participle) per rule 24, and both head on the lexical participle rather than on hath or is. Rule 86 licenses the supplied when in both: the participle is the source token carrying the subordination, so nothing here is added.
No article is left unrepresented: both ἡ tokens have an English the of their own, and no possessive or demonstrative competes for the slot, so rules 20, 38 and 49 do not reach this verse.

The one live head question is s011. bringeth was kept over forth because ἀποκυέω is glossed bring forth as a whole and bring is not an empty support verb of the make known / bear witness kind; the same lemma at JAS.1.18 should be headed on the verb word for consistency if that verse is aligned later.
δέ takes t010 and the second article takes t011 across the ASV's order; rule 15 covers the crossing and rule 26 keeps the article off its noun.
